title: Create public token packs
intent: Establish a frontend-owned public token contract that apps and built-ins can rely on without coupling appearance to schema. The first step is additive: create semantic `--ntx-*` tokens and keep current variable names alive through aliases so the existing UI keeps working during migration.
context: N3TX currently defines theme values directly in `dark-theme.css` and `light-theme.css`, and component CSS also references ad hoc names such as `--card-bg`, `--panel-bg`, and `--accent-primary`. This task creates the shared token foundation that later tasks will consume while keeping appearance entirely frontend-owned.
instructions: Create `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/styles/tokens/base.css`, `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/styles/tokens/dark.css`, and `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/styles/tokens/light.css`. In `base.css`, define the public semantic families for color, borders, glass, typography, spacing, radius, shadow, and motion, then alias legacy names like `--surface-0`, `--text-0`, `--accent`, `--border`, and `--radius-sm` to the new semantic values. In `dark.css` and `light.css`, override semantic tokens only; do not move body, button, or layout recipe styles into these files.
conventions: Use ASCII CSS, keep the naming public and semantic, and preserve backward compatibility by aliasing old names instead of deleting them. Token files should contain values and aliases, not component-specific layout rules.

checks: Base token file exposes a stable `--ntx-*` contract
Legacy variables are mapped to semantic tokens
Dark and light token files override semantic values only

title: Expand the theme runtime API
intent: The frontend needs a proper theme registry instead of a binary dark-light toggle helper so applications can patch tokens and compose future recipes without rewriting the framework helper. The existing toggle behavior must remain stable for current apps and tests.
context: `theme.js` currently stores `ntx-theme` in localStorage, updates `document.documentElement.dataset.theme`, and dispatches a `theme-change` event. That simple flow is useful and should remain the compatibility surface while new registration and token-patching helpers are added behind it.
instructions: Modify `/workspace/packages/n3tx-core/src/n3tx_core/static/utils/theme.js` to preserve `getTheme()`, `setTheme()`, and `toggleTheme()`, but add a small registry API for registering known theme names and optionally patching document-level CSS variables. Keep the storage key and dataset behavior unchanged, and keep the event payload compatible with current listeners while allowing extra detail fields if useful.
conventions: Do not break the current import-time auto-apply behavior. Keep the API tiny and framework-owned; this is a registry helper, not a full design system manager.

checks: Existing theme getter-setter-toggle semantics still work
Theme changes still update `data-theme` and dispatch `theme-change`
The module exposes additive registration helpers for future recipe work

title: Extract a reusable stylesheet loader
intent: N3TX needs one stylesheet loading path for all shadow-based UI, not separate implementations in Component, topbar, modal, sidebar, profile, and toast. A shared loader reduces drift, keeps caching behavior consistent, and gives later tasks one place to improve stylesheet adoption.
context: `Component.js` already caches and adopts CSSStyleSheets, but the implementation is private and unusable by standalone elements. Several framework components still inject `<link>` tags or maintain their own constructable stylesheet logic. This task turns the current logic into a reusable utility and keeps `Component` on the same behavior.
instructions: Create `/workspace/packages/n3tx-core/src/n3tx_core/static/core/stylesheets.js` with shared helpers for resolving one or many stylesheet URLs, fetching and caching constructable stylesheets, and adopting them onto a shadow root. Then update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-core/src/n3tx_core/static/core/Component.js` to use that helper instead of its private cache methods while preserving multi-stylesheet support and render deferral until styles are ready.
conventions: Preserve existing `get styles()` behavior, keep caching at module scope, and avoid flashes of unstyled shadow DOM. The utility should support arrays because stream and agent components already layer multiple stylesheets.

checks: Component still supports single or multiple stylesheet URLs
Constructable stylesheets are cached through the shared helper
Render scheduling still waits for styles to be ready

title: Bridge legacy theme entrypoints to tokens and a default recipe
intent: Existing apps load `dark-theme.css` and `light-theme.css` directly, so the new styling system must preserve those filenames while recutting them into token imports plus a default recipe. This task keeps the public loading contract stable while separating values from visuals.
context: The current theme files mix token definitions, page styling, body backgrounds, and component-adjacent skin rules. After task-01, token values should live in dedicated token packs; the remaining global look should move into a recipe file so future themes can compose different visuals with the same semantic contract.
instructions: Create `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/styles/recipes/glass/global.css` to hold the current framework-level visual recipe such as body ambiance, page chrome, typography defaults, and global button look. Then update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/dark-theme.css` to import `styles/tokens/base.css`, `styles/tokens/dark.css`, and the glass recipe, and update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/light-theme.css` to import `styles/tokens/light.css` and only light-mode overrides that truly depend on the `data-theme` switch.
conventions: Keep the legacy filenames and dataset-based switching intact. Recipes may be opinionated; token files should not be. Prefer imports and variable use over duplicating values.

checks: Dark and light entrypoints still load in existing HTML
Computed legacy variables still resolve because aliases exist
The default glass look now lives in a dedicated recipe file

title: Migrate shell components to the shared stylesheet loader
intent: Standalone shell components should use the same stylesheet cache and adoption path as `Component`-based elements so apps get consistent performance and customization behavior. This removes framework-level fragmentation without changing component responsibilities.
context: `ntx-topbar.js`, `ntx-sidebar.js`, and `ntx-profile.js` currently attach shadow roots and inject `<link>` elements or inline markup-level stylesheet tags. They are framework shell components, not data actors, but they still benefit from the same constructable stylesheet adoption used elsewhere.
instructions: Update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-topbar.js`, `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-sidebar.js`, and `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-profile.js` to import the shared stylesheet helper from `n3tx-core` static code. Remove their manual `<link>` management and adopt the relevant component CSS through the shared loader while preserving current render logic and lifecycle behavior.
conventions: Keep these components standalone; do not force them to inherit from `Component`. Use the shared loader as a utility only. Preserve current DOM and event behavior unless a style-loading bug requires a surgical adjustment.

title: Migrate modal and toast to the shared stylesheet loader
intent: Modal and toast currently use one-off stylesheet paths even though they are framework-level primitives used across the UI. Unifying them under the shared loader removes duplication and gives later theme work one consistent adoption path.
context: `ntx-modal.js` maintains its own constructable stylesheet singleton and `Toast.js` injects CSS into document head. Both pieces are UI infrastructure; they should share the same caching story as the rest of the framework while keeping their existing APIs intact.
instructions: Update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-modal.js` to use the shared stylesheet helper instead of its private sheet cache. Update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-core/src/n3tx_core/static/utils/Toast.js` to load `Toast.css` through the shared utility in a way that keeps the current global-toast UX intact, even if the implementation still ends in a document-level adoption step rather than a shadow root.
conventions: Keep `NTTModal.open()` and `showToast()` APIs stable. The goal is loader unification, not UX redesign. If Toast tests rely on implementation details, update them later in the dedicated test wave instead of forcing a brittle compatibility shim here.

title: Add base loading, error, and empty-state hooks
intent: A styling system is incomplete if components only skin happy-path rendering. The framework should own minimal loading, error, and empty defaults so apps can theme them instead of rebuilding them from scratch.
context: The frontend refactor notes already propose `renderLoading()`, `renderError(error)`, and `renderEmpty()` defaults in the `Component` base. `ntx-element.css` already contains base-state selectors but the base class does not expose a coherent state contract for theming and override.
instructions: Update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-core/src/n3tx_core/static/core/Component.js` to provide default `renderLoading()`, `renderError(error)`, and `renderEmpty()` helpers and a lightweight `data-state` contract that subclasses can reuse. Update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-element.css` to rename or extend the state selectors so they consume semantic tokens and match the new base class output without forcing a specific visual recipe.
conventions: Defaults should be minimal and overridable. Do not make base states visually loud; expose a contract that recipe CSS and app CSS can restyle. Preserve the current abstract `render()` flow and do not force data fetching decisions into `Component`.

title: Make widget stylesheet adoption explicit
intent: Widget styling currently depends on implicit global CSS assumptions even though widgets render inside shadow roots. The framework needs an explicit widget stylesheet contract so widget visuals travel with the components that use them.
context: `widgets.css` defines many classes used by widget renderers, but the stylesheet is not systematically adopted by shadow components that render widget output. `ntx-item` and row-based editing surfaces are the main framework-owned widget hosts and should intentionally layer widget styles into their `styles` arrays.
instructions: Update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/widgets/index.js` to export the shared widget stylesheet URL list, including `widgets.css` and any other shared widget CSS that should be adopted by hosts. Then update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-item.js` and `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-row.js` so their `get styles()` return inherited component CSS plus the exported widget stylesheet URLs.
conventions: Do not couple widget adoption to global document CSS. Keep the contract simple: widgets export the styles they need, and widget-host components opt into those URLs by composition.

title: Expose stable styling surfaces on entity components
intent: Apps should be able to restyle `ntx-item` and `ntx-list` without replacing them or targeting brittle internal selectors. Stable `part` names and host/state attributes are the main customization contract for shadow components.
context: `ntx-item` and `ntx-list` are the core entity renderers used throughout the framework. They already control their own markup and display modes; this task makes that markup intentionally stylable by exposing semantic parts such as container, title, fields, actions, and empty states.
instructions: Update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-item.js` and `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-list.js` so the key DOM nodes receive stable `part` names and meaningful host or root state attributes such as `data-state`, `display`, and `mode`. Keep current behavior and display-mode dispatch intact; the change should be surgical markup annotation rather than a render rewrite.
conventions: Use role-based part names, not DOM-shape names. The public contract should describe semantics like title, field, and actions rather than implementation details like div-1 or header-row. Do not break current event binding or display mode logic.

title: Expose stable styling surfaces on action and stream components
intent: Method buttons and streaming views are public primitives too, and they need the same restyling contract as item and list components. Stable parts let apps theme action forms, stream outputs, and agent streams without forking framework code.
context: `ntx-method`, `ntx-stream`, and `ntx-stream-agent` currently render their own shadow DOM but do not expose a supported styling surface. The streaming hierarchy already layers stylesheets; this task adds semantic parts and state attributes to those same renderers.
instructions: Update `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-method.js`, `/workspace/packages/n3tx-ui/src/n3tx_ui/static/components/ntx-stream.js`, and `/workspace/packages/n3tx-agents/src/n3tx_agents/static/components/ntx-stream-agent.js` so their rendered DOM exposes semantic `part` names and stable state attributes for forms, buttons, output containers, stream entries, and footers. Preserve current method execution and stream dispatch behavior.
conventions: Keep the stream inheritance chain additive. Annotate markup and state rather than re-architecting stream behavior. Use semantic parts like form, input, output, entry, and footer.

context: `ntx-item.css`, `ntx-list.css`, and `ntx-method.css` currently lean on a mix of legacy variables and local fallback values.
